title: Edward Clem and the Eagle band
summary: Morris remembers cornetist Edward Clem, who wore an eye pad and played in Frankie Dusen's Eagle band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you ever hear of Edward Clem?
Yeah. Edward Clem used to play cornet. He used to wear eyeglass.
Well, he was good. Edward Clem was good, too.
Was he a musician? Yeah, Edward Clem.
He used to wear, he had one eye out, I think. They used to wear a little pad on one of them eyes.
But he could read? Or was he a barber head man?
I don't know. He was, he would always get good men. Edward Clem used to play at Frankie Dewson, too. That's right. Edward Clem used to play at Frankie Dewson.
What was the name of the band then?
Yeah, well, I figured we'd get him around doing the band.
Yeah, that's right. We thought of it. Yeah, it was the Eagle Band.
Yeah, that was a cornet player.
Uh-huh, he was rock climbing. He was really a cornet player.
